questions.q: Is there a single AWS product called "Data Lake" that you provision?
options: No — a data lake is an architecture pattern built from S3 plus a catalog and query layer on top
Yes — it's a managed service you enable on an S3 bucket
Yes — it's part of the Glue console
No — data lakes require a third-party product, AWS has no equivalent
questions.explain: AWS has no single 'Data Lake' product. The pattern is composed from S3 storage, the Glue Data Catalog for schema, and Athena or Redshift Spectrum for querying.

questions.q: In the raw / staged / curated zone convention, what does the 'raw' (bronze) zone hold?
options: Data exactly as it arrived from the source, untouched
Fully cleaned and business-ready modeled data
Only data that failed validation checks
Data already loaded into Redshift tables
questions.explain: The raw/bronze zone preserves data exactly as it arrived, unmodified — so the source can always be reprocessed if something downstream goes wrong.

questions.q: What is the role of the Glue Data Catalog in this architecture?
options: A metadata store recording each table's location in S3, its columns/types, and its partitions
A compute engine that runs the actual SQL queries
A storage class for infrequently accessed S3 objects
An IAM policy type used only for cross-account access
questions.explain: The Glue Data Catalog is the metadata layer — it doesn't store data itself, but records schema and location information that lets Athena and Redshift Spectrum query S3 as if it were a database.

questions.q: Why does keeping an untouched raw zone matter if a malformed export corrupts staged data?
options: Because staged/curated data can be reprocessed from the raw zone, which was never modified
It doesn't matter — raw data is deleted automatically after staging completes
Raw zone data is always more accurate than staged data
Raw zone data is the only zone Athena can query
questions.explain: Since raw data is kept exactly as it arrived and never mutated, teams can always reprocess from raw to regenerate staged/curated data after a bug or bad transform, rather than losing the original source.

questions.q: Which two services does this lesson name as able to query S3 data directly via the Glue Catalog, without a separate load step?
options: Athena and Redshift Spectrum
Lambda and Step Functions
IAM and CloudTrail
EMR and Kinesis only
questions.explain: Athena runs SQL directly against S3 via the Glue Catalog billed per TB scanned, and Redshift Spectrum lets a Redshift cluster query S3 data the same way, joining it with data already loaded in Redshift.
